feature: Remediation Tracking: 28-step programme - the real artifacts/portal '/remediation-tracking' page (src/pages/remediation-tracking.tsx), part of #3037/#3039/Feature #1489. Wires GET /api/portal/remediation-tracker (steps + live pricing), PUT /api/portal/remediation-tracker/steps/:stepId, POST .../steps/:stepId/verify, GET .../steps/:stepId/verification-guide, POST .../steps/:stepId/decline-to-risk (§1a, #3037), plus GET .../pillar-scores and the export.csv/export.pdf/evidence-pack.pdf downloads (§1f-1g, #3039 - PillarScoresCard + RemediationExportControls, both mounted inside RemediationProgrammeTab on this same tab), per docs/portal/remediation-tracking-contract-pack.md and the landed 'Remediation Tracking.dc.html' export's 28-step programme tab. Does NOT cover the checklist/fix-routes/reveal/bypass-resolutions tabs (§1b-1e, #3038) - a separate real functional unit under the same Feature, still in flight as of this edit.
notes: WHAT THIS COVERS: the auth gate on every §1a route, the real 200 payload shape (steps[] + pricing.phases[3]/pricing.hire), the explicit 400 §1a's PUT returns when a client tries to set accepted_risk directly (the signed-only guard), 400s for an unknown stepId across PUT/verify/verification-guide, a 404 for verification-guide on a step with no mapped check, a real, REVERSIBLE PUT round-trip (unlike Risk Register's accept, a status PUT is not a permanent signed action, so the write is undone at the end of the same test run to keep this manifest idempotent), and a real UI walk (login -> open the programme tab) proving the #3039 pillar scores card actually renders real data for a signed-in customer.

WHY NO decline-to-risk HAPPY PATH IS DRIVEN HERE: same reason risk-register.json's own accept step is not driven - POST .../decline-to-risk creates a PERMANENT signed msp_risk_decisions row and 409s on a second attempt against the same step (§1a). Exercising it for real would either poison this manifest's re-runs or require a live SQL reset step outside the manifest's own scope. The 400 surface on the sibling PUT route (the same signed-only guard) is exercised instead, which is what proves the underlying contract.

AUTH CORE HAS LANDED (#2991, Feature #1648) - login.tsx now ships real #email/#password inputs and a login-submit testid, so this manifest drives a real login and asserts the real rendered pillar-scores card instead of only the pre-auth honest empty state (Git #4104 - this note previously said no login page existed yet; that premise was stale, the same correction test-manifests/portal/risk-register.json already made).

shaneapp://runTest WAS ACTUALLY INVOKED (2026-09-06, session for #3037), not skipped by assumption - two real attempts, both against this manifest AND against the pre-existing test-manifests/portal/risk-register.json (bare filename and full repo-relative path), all four returned the identical real envelope `{ ok:false, error:'manifest not found or unparseable: <file>' }`. Root cause confirmed directly, not guessed: BuildConsole's dev-server checkout (default `C:\dev-server`) is on branch `dev-server` at commit 145ba36ad - `git log` there shows no test-manifests/ directory at all yet, hundreds of commits behind the origin/main HEAD this build pushes to (c51abcdf0 at push time). This is the SAME structural gap #3004's/#2996's/#2998's manifests already document (dev-server hasn't merged/restarted onto a current checkout), just with concrete evidence of exactly how stale rather than an assumption - not a runTest defect, and not specific to this file. Verified instead by a real `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` pass (0 errors) and a real `vite build` (succeeds) against artifacts/portal with this page/route/hooks added, plus direct reading of portal-remediation-tracker.ts confirming every status/error shape asserted below. Re-run via shaneapp://runTest once the dev-server merge/restart cycle has caught up.
